title: Average Treatment Effect Localization: Projection Methods in Synthetic Control
abstract: arXiv:2609.10617v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Many real-world policies and business interventions require assessing short-term effects to inform timely decisions, even though most causal inference methods focus on long-term average treatment effects. In this paper, we introduce average treatment effect localization (ATEL), which captures localized, short-term policy impacts in panel data settings with a single treated unit and provides early indicators of policy impact. To accommodate both time-varying and nonlinear effects of observed and unobserved covariates, we propose a nonparametric model for untreated outcome, interpreted as a time-varying factor model via sieve approximation. Estimating the time-varying factor model is challenging due to the boundary bias and identification. Our estimation method based on diversified projection can effectively address these issues. translated_title: 平均处理效应定位：合成控制中的投影方法
translated_abstract: 许多现实世界的政策和商业干预措施需要评估短期效应以便及时做出决策，然而大多数因果推断方法关注的是长期平均处理效应。在本文中，我们提出了平均处理效应定位（ATEL）方法，该方法能够在包含单个处理单元的面板数据环境中捕捉局部化的、短期的政策影响，并提供政策影响的早期指标。为了适应观测变量和未观测变量的时变和非线性效应，我们针对未处理结果提出了一个非参数模型，并通过筛近似将其解释为时变因子模型。由于边界偏差和识别问题，估计时变因子模型具有挑战性。我们提出的基于多样化投影的估计方法可以有效解决这些问题。我们发展了渐近分布理论，以便对ATEL估计量进行统计推断。在一个实证应用中……
tldr: 本文提出平均处理效应定位（ATEL）方法，通过基于多样化投影的非参数时变因子模型，在单个处理单元的面板数据中捕捉短期局部化政策影响，并建立了渐近分布理论以支持统计推断。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Average Treatment Effect Localization (ATEL), which uses a diversified projection-based nonparametric time-varying factor model to capture localized short-term policy impacts in panel data with a single treated unit, supported by asymptotic distribution theory for statistical inference.
